target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

Tools that may yield must declare `executionMode: "sequential"`. Agent-core inspects that declaration before starting the batch, so a successful yield aborts the turn before later sibling tools run. A yield result from a default/parallel tool is rejected before the runtime control handler is invoked. Sequential tools remain model-visible and are excluded from Tool Search, Code Mode, and headless catalogs because those outer bridges cannot preserve the target tool's pre-execution scheduling identity.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration; only tools that opt into yield must declare sequential execution.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.
- Require yielding tools to declare `executionMode: "sequential"` and reject incompatible results.
- Stop a sequential batch after yield so later side-effectful sibling tools never start.
- Keep sequential tools on the direct execution surface instead of hiding them behind Tool Search, Code Mode, or headless catalogs.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization, scheduling, and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are the values applied by the runtime.
- Agent-core tests prove an unsupported finalized control becomes an explicit tool error.
- Agent-core tests prove a non-sequential yielding tool is rejected before its control handler runs.
- Agent-core tests prove a sequential yielding tool prevents a later side-effectful sibling from starting.
- Catalog tests prove sequential tools remain direct across Tool Search and Code Mode and are omitted from headless catalogs.
- Embedded orchestration coverage proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

### Verification

- Scheduler TDD RED: CI run `29575710823` failed the new non-sequential-yield assertion before the guard existed.
- Scheduler TDD GREEN: the same Node shard passed in CI run `29576120720` after the guard was added.
- Catalog TDD RED: CI run `29577281682`, job `87874669293`, failed all three new assertions because sequential tools were still hidden by Tool Search, Code Mode, and headless catalogs.
- Catalog TDD GREEN: exact-head CI run `29578038838` passed after sequential tools were restricted to direct execution.
- Exact head `f3ce089ae9404fba3d745238948bf08493f7d46a` is rebased on `main` commit `6745f9a553283c1c75d31cc123b8c85d76407399`.
- Exact-head CI: 55 successful jobs, 11 conditional skips, 0 failures, 0 pending.
- `build-artifacts`, Plugin SDK declarations/surface checks, docs, lint, production types, test types, all selected Node shards, CodeQL, OpenGrep, and workflow sanity passed.
- `git diff --check` passes.
